attributes.body_ja:
「につき」は「に」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「就（つ）く」でできている文型（ぶんけい）で、たいていの場合（ばあい）はひらがなで書（か）かれます。動詞（どうし）の「就（つ）く」は「引（ひ）き受（う）ける」や「身（み）を置（お）く」という意味（いみ）を持（も）ち、よく新（あたら）しい仕事（しごと）、地位（ちい）や立場（たちば）などと関連（かんれん）して使（つか）われます。

しかし、この文型（ぶんけい）はふつう「(A) の理由（りゆう）で (B)」「(A) が原因（げんいん）で (B)」「(A) ごとに (B)」などの意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。「につき」は名詞（めいし）の後（うし）ろに直接（ちょくせつ）置（お）かれ、その後（うし）ろの (B) の部分（ぶぶん）で (A) が理由（りゆう）や原因（げんいん）となって起（お）こっている内容（ないよう）の説明（せつめい）が続（つづ）きます。

「につき」はとても硬（かた）い文型（ぶんけい）なので、正式（せいしき）な書類（しょるい）や公（おおやけ）の場（ば）での告知（こくち）、または通知（つうち）などで使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

この文法（ぶんぽう）の根底（こんてい）にある「(A) に付（つ）く」という意味（いみ）は、「につき」の全（すべ）ての用法（ようほう）に共通（きょうつう）していると言（い）えます。というのも、(B) の内容（ないよう）は、(A) に対応（たいおう）するもの、(A) に適（てき）したもの、(A) と直接（ちょくせつ）繋（つな）がるもの、または (A) によって引（ひ）き起（お）こされるものになり、どれも (A) と (B) が密接（みっせつ）に関連（かんれん）しているというニュアンスを持（も）つためです。
attributes.body:
Although rarely seen in its kanji form, につき is a grammar pattern that comes from a combination of に and the conjunctive form of the う- Verb 就（つ）く 'to take up (A)', or 'to assume (A)'. This meaning is usually in regard to assuming a new position, such as a new job.

However, the particular meaning conveyed here will be closer to 'due to (A), (B)', 'on account of (A), (B)', or 'for each (A), (B)'. につき will follow nouns directly, before the (B) part of the sentence describes what is happening 'due to' or 'on account of (A)'.

This grammar point is quite formal, so it is often seen in formal documents, announcements, and notifications.

Regardless of the several common English translations, the base meaning of 'to affix to (A)' is kept in all of the uses of につき, as it simply implies that (B) is in answer to, exists in a way that is directly linked to, suitable for, or caused by (A).

Both せいで and につき express cause, but with different nuance and tone. せいで is more colloquial and typically introduces a cause for a negative result, e.g. 雨のせいで試合が中止になった ('The game was canceled because of the rain.'). につき states a reason more neutrally and is often used in formal written announcements, e.g. 工事中につき通行止め ('Closed to traffic due to construction.').

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: Both are formal expressions where one condition influences another, but with different nuance. につき means on account of or due to, as in 雨天につき中止になる (Cancelled due to rain). にあたり・にあたって means on the occasion of or at the time of, as in 退職にあたり一言挨拶をする (Say a few words on the occasion of retiring).

first_relatable.title: につき
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

second_relatable.title: にあたり・にあたって
second_relatable.meaning: When, When doing something, On the occasion, At the time

attributes.body: Both express cause, but differ in tone and formality. おかげで implies a positive result with gratitude, e.g. 先生のおかげで合格できました ('Thanks to my teacher, I passed.') につき states a neutral reason, often used in formal notices, e.g. 雨天につき中止します ('Due to rain, it is canceled.') It also only follows nouns.

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: These expressions are loosely related in that both indicate a reason. ばかりに conveys that a specific cause led to a negative outcome, often with a nuance of regret, e.g. 忘れ物をしたばかりに受験できなかった ('Just because I forgot something, I couldn't take the exam'). につき, by contrast, is a formal, neutral expression often used in official contexts, e.g. 工事中につき通行止め ('Road closed due to construction').

first_relatable.title: ばかりに
first_relatable.meaning: Simply because, Only because, Just because, Simply on account of

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: Both ために and につき can express 'due to (A)', but differ in tone and usage. ために requires の to connect to nouns, e.g. 悪天候のため ('Due to bad weather') につき connects directly and sounds stiffer or more formal, e.g. 悪天候につき (Same meaning) Unlike ために, につき cannot be used to express purpose.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: Though similar in that both use に with a form of the verb つく, these patterns differ in meaning and formality level. について means 'concerning (A)' and typically marks the topic of a discussion, question, or so forth, e.g. 日本文化について話す ('Talk about Japanese culture'), while につき is a formal way to express a reason or condition, often used in official announcements, e.g. 悪天候につき中止する ('Cancel due to bad weather').

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: まい～のように and につき both express frequency, but in different ways. まい～のように is used with 'every~' time expressions to mean 'almost every (A)', e.g. 毎日のように 'almost every day'. In contrast, につき follows time/quantity expressions to mean 'each' or 'every,' e.g. 30分につき 'for every 30 minutes'. につき can also mean 'due to', which is unrelated to frequency.
